chemistry.formulae-practical-items.0010.all: Mass of empty crucible + lid; mass of crucible + lid + metal; mass of crucible + lid + oxide after heating to constant mass.

chemistry.group1-describe-items.0011.all: Lithium reacts less vigorously / slower fizzing; does not melt into a ball and no flame (potassium bursts into lilac flame).

chemistry.group1-explain-items.0009.all: Atoms/ions get larger down the group; weaker attraction between the positive ions and delocalised electrons, so less energy needed to melt.

chemistry.group1-recall-facts.0004.all: Sodium hydroxide is formed, which releases OH- ions.

chemistry.group1-trend-data.0004.a: Melting point decreases down the group.
chemistry.group1-trend-data.0004.c: Potassium is less dense than sodium (density does not increase steadily).

chemistry.group7-displacement-eq.0019.b: Chlorine (Cl2) is reduced; it gains electrons (forms Cl-).

chemistry.group7-explain-items.0011.a: Bromine is less reactive than chlorine, so it cannot displace chloride / chlorine from KCl.
chemistry.group7-explain-items.0011.b: Not on spec to explain; would say colour pattern pale yellow (F) -> green -> red-brown -> grey-black as molecules get larger.

chemistry.group7-practical-items.0001.all: Add each halogen solution to solutions of the other halides (KCl, KBr, KI); look for colour change; colour change means the halogen is more reactive and has displaced the halide; chlorine displaces Br and I, bromine displaces I only, iodine none: Cl > Br > I.

chemistry.group7-trend-data.0007.a: Boiling point increases down the group.
chemistry.group7-trend-data.0007.c: Solid; melting point increases down the group so astatine's mp is well above room temperature.

chemistry.ionic-describe-formation.0015.all: Each Li atom loses its 1 outer electron; each Br atom gains 1 electron; transfer from Li to Br; forming Li+ and Br- ions with full outer shells (held by electrostatic attraction).

chemistry.ionic-explain-items.0002.all: Giant ionic lattice; strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged Mg2+ and O2- ions; lots of energy needed to overcome.

chemistry.metallic-explain-items.0003.all: Contains delocalised electrons, which can move through the structure carrying charge.

chemistry.metallic-mcq-facts.0010.all: able to be drawn into wires

chemistry.metallic-recall-facts.0010.all: Strong electrostatic attraction between positive ions and delocalised electrons needs much energy to overcome.
